source_title: HUGEL's Kolkata gig aims to put the city on India's concert tourism map - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Kolkata could be gearing up for an unconventional Christmas celebration this year, with international DJ HUGEL set to perform in the city on December 25. The gig is being planned at an unusual venue that has never hosted a live music event before. While the venue is yet to be officially confirmed, the larger ambition behind the event goes beyond a single night of music: to put Kolkata on India's growing concert tourism map.For Saksham Mohta, who is spearheading the initiative, large-scale live events can play an important role in bringing visitors to the city, encouraging them to explore its food, culture and hospitality alongside attending a concert. The idea is to make Kolkata a destination that people travel to for live entertainment, rather than one that music enthusiasts routinely leave behind for concerts in other metros."People should not have to travel to Mumbai, Bengaluru or Delhi to watch their favourite artists. I want Kolkata to have its own scene when it comes to hosting some of the biggest names in music," says Saksham, who was born and brought up in the city.The December 25 date also has a personal significance for him, as it coincides with his birthday. With Christmas being one of Kolkata's biggest festive occasions, he wanted to mark the day by bringing an international act to the city."I wanted to give back to the city. December 25 is Christmas, which Kolkata celebrates on such a large scale, and it is also my birthday. I thought this would be a good way to bring something special to the city," he says.Can concerts drive tourism?Concert-led travel, or gig tourism, has become an increasingly visible part of India's live entertainment economy, with audiences travelling between cities for major performances. Mohta hopes the HUGEL show will draw music fans from neighbouring states and beyond, giving them an opportunity to explore Kolkata while attending the concert.However, he says the availability of suitable venues remains a major challenge for organisers looking to bring international acts to the city. "The biggest issue in Kolkata is the venue. We do not have enough venues, and most artists are hesitant to come here because the infrastructure is not quite at par with other cities," he says.Mohta hopes to make the December 25 concert an annual event and organise more shows on other important dates. He acknowledges that the cost of bringing international performers makes it difficult to ensure profitability, but says his immediate focus is on building a live music audience in the city."I'm doing this for the city, for the passion of the scene and for the people. I don't want to make money on my birthday. I want to do something for the city, which has given me so much," he says.From Tomorrowland to CoachellaHUGEL has performed at international music festivals including Tomorrowland, EDC Las Vegas, EDC Mexico and Parookaville. In 2026, he made his Coachella debut at the Sahara Tent and opened for David Guetta at the Stade de France in Paris.
